description: ArtifactsBench is a large-scale benchmark of 1,825 diverse tasks for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual code generation. It covers nine domains (e.g., web, SVG, games, simulations) stratified into Easy/Medium/Hard tiers, and uses an automated multimodal evaluation pipeline that renders artifacts, captures three-step temporal screenshots, and scores them with a checklist-guided MLLM-as-Judge.
name: ArtifactsBench
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each query is paired with one 10-dimension checklist. For human validation, 280 queries were independently scored by multiple front-end engineers, with the final ground-truth score being the median of individual annotators' ratings.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Human validators were engineers with extensive front-end development experience. The study used a double-blind protocol with randomized sample ordering to mitigate bias.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement on the 10% manually curated seed achieves Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8. For automated vs. human agreement, pairwise consistency (Pair ACC) was measured on 280 queries across 6 models; Gemini-2.5-Pro achieved up to 90.95% pairwise agreement with human experts.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists are LLM-drafted and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchors calibration and achieves Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators; the seed is reused as few-shot references. Difficulty is assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models with a target 30%/40%/30% Easy/Medium/Hard split.
rai:dataBiases: Automated filters explicitly removed license-violating, duplicate, trivial, and non-interactive items to reduce bias toward static or low-quality content. A double-blind annotation protocol with randomized sample ordering was used to mitigate annotator bias. The benchmark prioritizes dynamics (state changes, animations, responsiveness) which may underrepresent purely static visual tasks.
rai:dataCollection: Tasks were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots. Automated filters removed incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity/completeness/executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw candidates sourced from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM-generated visual-to-query pairs from screenshots.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Others
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark evaluates dynamic behavior via discrete screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture fluidity, correctness, and robustness of complex long-horizon or state-dependent interactions. It focuses on single-turn artifact generation and does not assess agentic, iterative, or multi-turn development capabilities. The MLLM referee can suffer from hallucination, prompt sensitivity, limited awareness of engineering/code quality, and version drift.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Difficulty tiers (Easy/Medium/Hard) were assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ LLMs to enforce a 30%/40%/30% split; realized split was 559/611/655. Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks. Prompts were rewritten by experts and LLMs for diversity and clarity.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two-stage deduplication and contamination control: (i) MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings are released; future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains.
rai:dataSocialImpact: ArtifactsBench provides a scalable, automated evaluation tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models, enabling more reliable assessment of LLMs for real-world interactive web applications. It bridges the gap between automated benchmarks and human preferences, supporting progress in AI-assisted software creation.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating LLMs on their ability to generate high-quality interactive visual artifacts (web widgets, data visualizations, mini-games, SVG graphics); benchmarking and ranking LLMs for visual code generation; providing fine-grained diagnostics on model strengths and failure modes; accelerating development of user-centric generative models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini-2.5-Pro (used for checklist generation, query classification, and as MLLM-as-Judge referee); Qwen2.5-VL-72B (used as open-source MLLM-as-Judge referee); Hunyuan-Turbos (used for checklist generation); GPT-o4-mini (used as referee in ablation studies); MinHash (for deduplication); perceptual hashing (for screenshot deduplication); a lightweight classifier for sub-category tagging.

evidence.name: we introduce ArtifactsBench, a benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation.
evidence.description: We curate 1,825 diverse tasks and evaluate over 30 leading LLMs. Our automated evaluation achieves 94.4% ranking consistency with WebDev Arena—a de facto gold standard for human preferences in web development—and up to 90.95% pairwise agreement with human experts.
